title: QBR Slimline Deck + Renewal Tactics (Standard & Enterprise Variants)
body:
Purpose:
This is a slim, high-impact QBR deck template paired with a lightweight renewal tactics playbook and a one-page renewal tracker. Purpose is to give CSMs a repeatable, fast-to-customize kit for both standard (SMB / mid-market) and enterprise accounts where time-to-insight and a clear renewal plan matter.

Audience:
- Primary: Customer Success Managers and Renewal Owners
- Secondary: Solutions Engineers, Account Execs, Customer Success Leadership

How to use this file:
- Copy the slimline slide list into Google Slides and replace the placeholders.
- Use the "Standard" path for accounts under $50k ARR or low-complexity integrations; use the "Enterprise" path when security, multi-team adoption, or procurement complexity is present.
- Attach the renewal tracker snapshot (text table below) to the follow-up email within 48 hours.

Slide list (single-slide notes):
1) Cover + One-line Impact
   - Slide content: Customer name, period (QX YYYY), one-line outcome statement (what success looks like).
   - Speaker note: Open with 30s recap of partnership theme.

2) Top-line Health Snapshot (1/2 page)
   - Metrics: ARR coverage, usage change (% tokens/requests), SLA incidents (count), adoption score (1-10).
   - Visual: 3 small chips (Health, Usage Trend, Support).
   - Speaker note: Call out one leading indicator and one risk.

3) What we delivered this quarter (3 bullets + impact)
   - Focus on outcomes tied to customer goals.
   - Speaker note: Tie each bullet to ROI or operational improvement.

4) Feature adoption map (who uses what)
   - Rows: Teams / personas; Columns: Features (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console features used).
   - Speaker note: Surface three opportunity owners to scale usage.

5) Quality & Cost summary (one slide)
   - Key stats: Avg latency, cost per 1k tokens, model variants in use, any regression alerts.
   - Speaker note: If cost is rising, propose batching/quantization pilot.

6) Enterprise-add (only for Enterprise variant) - Security & Compliance posture
   - Include: Audit log status, VPC/private controls, KMS/HSM integration state, pending certs.
   - Speaker note: Confirm procurement next steps and timelines.

7) Renewal health & ask (dual-path)
   - Standard variant: Clear renewal ask + one prioritized value add (e.g., additional developer seats).
   - Enterprise variant: Renewal ask + procurement timeline + two-step pilot/POC extension if needed.

8) Risk matrix & mitigation (one slide)
   - Rows: Risk (cost, security, performance, adoption), Columns: Likelihood (Low/Med/High), Mitigation owner/action.
   - Speaker note: Commit specific owners and timelines in the meeting.

9) Action plan (30/60/90 days) + owners
   - 30 day: Quick wins, 60 day: integrations/rollout, 90 day: ROI measurement.
   - Speaker note: End with a commitment request (calendar invite for kickoffs).

10) Appendix (optional tech notes + eval snapshots)
   - Include links to performance traces, error breakdowns, cost breakdowns per route.

Renewal tracker (one-page text template to copy into sheet or doc):
Columns: Account, ARR, Renewal date, Current term, Owner, Risk level (Low/Med/High), Blocking issues, Next action, Due date, Notes
Example row (text):
- "Acme Retail, $120,000, 2025-09-15, Annual, Jun Park, Medium, Procurement requires SOC2, Schedule security checklist by 2025-03-10, SE to confirm cert status"

Renewal playbook (actionable steps, concise):
- T-minus 90 days: Health email + invite to QBR, attach slimline preview. Owner: CSM.
- T-minus 60 days: Exec align call (15m) for enterprise / standard exec summary for SMB. Owner: AE + CSM.
- T-minus 45 days: Risk remediation sprint begins (solutions engineer + customer). Owner: SE.
- T-minus 30 days: Final commercial ask sent (term options + incentives). Owner: CSM + Sales Ops.
- Post-renewal: Onboarding/rollout plan scheduled (30/60/90 checkpoints). Owner: CSM.

Sample scripts (short):
- Opening to execs: "We ran the numbers this quarter — your team saw X% faster inference and Y% cost reduction on route Z. For renewals, we want to ensure we lock in performance while reducing per-token spend; we propose a 12-month commitment with a pilot for quantized model to cut costs 15%"
- Objection handling (procurement wants SOC2): "We're tracking SOC2 completion for your environment — here's the owner and target date; as a mitigation we can provide an interim segregated environment + audit artifact pack to speed procurement."

Risk mitigation matrix (text):
- Cost spike: Likelihood Medium; Mitigation: Enable prefix caching + recommend batching policy; Owner: Platform eng SE; ETA: 21 days.
- Security questions: Likelihood High for enterprise; Mitigation: Provide audit artifacts and KMS plan + escalation to compliance lead; Owner: Solutions Eng; ETA: 14 days.
- Slow adoption: Likelihood Medium; Mitigation: Run two-hour enablement workshops + playbook for product teams; Owner: CSM; ETA: 30 days.

Customization notes (quick):
- Use the Standard variant when account ARR < $50k or fewer than 3 technical stakeholders. Keep slides 6-8 only.
- Use the Enterprise variant when procurement, security, or multi-team rollout are present. Add slide 6 and keep appendix.

Follow-up checklist (after meeting):
- Send meeting notes + attached renewal tracker snapshot within 48 hours.
- Assign owners in CRM and flag next action.
- Attach any required security docs and update linked artifacts.
- Schedule follow-up 30/60 day checkpoints.

Metrics to highlight in each QBR (recommended KPIs):
- ARR coverage and change from last QBR (absolute and %).
- API call volume and tokens per request distribution.
- Avg latency (p50/p95) and error rate.
- Cost per 1k tokens and impact of any optimization pilot.
- Adoption: number of active users / teams and percent of seats used.

Folder checklist before sending to customer:
- Ensure slide 6 (security) has updated status for enterprise customers.
- Include a one-line "ask" on the renewal slide with two alternative commercial options (12-month standard, 12-month + pilot).
- Validate any technical claims against the performance traces linked in Confluence.

Notes & open questions (for internal use):
- Should we standardize an offer for "quantization pilot" as an incentive on renewals? Pros/cons to discuss with pricing.
- Consider a 1-pager SOC2 summary extract specifically for QBRs to reduce procurement friction.

Owner notes: Aisha Patel — initial draft. Please use this slimline deck for quick QBRs; iterate with local SEs for enterprise customers.
